newsitem.title: USA: 3 ex-ADM execs plead not guilty in antitrust case.
newsitem.headline: 3 ex-ADM execs plead not guilty in antitrust case.

text.p: Three former Archer Daniels Midland Co executives on Thursday pleaded not guilty in federal court to charges that they conspired to fix prices of lysine, a feed additive.

An executive of Ajinomoto Co Inc of Japan, who had also been charged with price fixing, did not appear in court today. Prosecutors said Kazutoshi Yamada of Ajinomoto did not accept U.S. jurisdiction in the case.
Appearing in court today were Michael Andreas, former vice chairman of ADM; Terrance Wilson, former group vice president; and Mark Whitacre, who had headed ADM's BioProducts Division.
None of the defendants made statements in court.
The three defendants were released on $4,500 bond each. Whitacre, however, was required to surrender his U.S. passport, prohibiting him from INTERRUPTED
Whitacre had acted as a government informant for three years in the case brought against ADM. Earlier this month, however, Whitacre said he would no longer cooperate with the U.S. government.

Whitacre was fired from ADM, which claimed he stole about $9.0 million from it. Whitacre has denied the charge, saying he received about $6.5 million in off-the-books bonuses that allegedly were approved by ADM management. He has said some of that money is in foreign accounts.
